tex_content.html:
Proposition
Source: topping:page-0068, topping:page-0069 1. ch6:1.1\group topping-gradient-flow The $L^2$-gradient of the total scalar curvature is \[ \nabla E(g)=\frac{R}{2}g-\Ric . \] If the metric formally follows the upward gradient flow \[ \frac{\partial g}{\partial t}=\frac{R}{2}g-\Ric , \] then \[ \frac{\partial R}{\partial t} =-\left(\frac{n}{2}-1\right)\Delta R+|\Ric |^2-\frac12R^2. \tag {6.1.1} \]

Proof

\sketch For $h=\partial _tg$, the first variation is

\[ \frac{d}{dt}E(g)=\int _{\mathcal M} \left\langle \frac{R}{2}g-\Ric ,h\right\rangle dV, \]

after the divergence terms integrate to zero. Substitution of $h=\frac{R}{2}g-\Ric $ into the scalar-curvature variation formula, together with $\delta \Ric +\frac12dR=0$, gives the displayed evolution equation.

□

For $n\geq 3$, the leading term in this scalar-curvature equation has the backward-heat sign, so the upward gradient equation is not generally a forward well-posed evolution from arbitrary initial metrics.
